note: Day-2 calibration set. Anchors are hand-written: cliche = what a chatbot says first, mid = a known idea with a real twist, far = workable but well outside the usual answer space. Targets: cliche >= 70, mid 30-70, far <= 35.

prompts.prompt: Suggest a side business for a software developer
cliche: Build a SaaS product for small businesses
Create and sell an online programming course
mid: Offer fixed-price accessibility audits for local government websites
Sell pre-configured home-lab kits for privacy-minded families
far: Rent yourself out as a code archaeologist who documents abandoned legacy systems for insurance audits
Breed rare aquarium shrimp and sell them through a self-built auction bot

prompts.prompt: How can a small coffee shop attract more customers?
cliche: Offer free Wi-Fi and comfortable seating
mid: Host a monthly cupping night where regulars vote on next month's bean
Partner with the nearest coworking space for a shared membership
far: Become the neighbourhood's lost-and-found and parcel drop, so people come in for errands
Let customers pay by fixing one item from the shop's broken-things shelf

prompts.prompt: Give me a fresh idea for a birthday party for a 10-year-old
cliche: Have a pizza and movie night sleepover
mid: Run a backyard escape room built around the child's favourite book
Host a mini bake-off judged by grandparents over video call
far: Turn the party into a one-day newspaper: kids interview neighbours and print an edition
Guests arrive as clients of a fake detective agency and must solve who ate the cake

prompts.prompt: Name ideas for a new productivity app
mid: Tomorrow Me
Small Hours
far: Mudroom
Third Coffee

prompts.prompt: How can a city reduce traffic congestion?
mid: Stagger school and office start times by district
Pay employers per employee who switches to a four-day office week
far: Auction the right to deliver parcels in each district to one carrier per day
Turn traffic lights into a reward system: drivers who skip peak hours earn parking credits

prompts.prompt: Suggest a marketing campaign for a new running shoe
cliche: Offer a discount for the first 100 buyers
mid: Give the shoe to night-shift nurses and publish their step counts
Let runners trade in worn shoes for credit and show the wear map
far: Release the shoe only to people who finish a route drawn as the brand logo on a city map
Sponsor the slowest finisher of every local race

prompts.prompt: Ideas to improve employee engagement in a remote team
mid: Rotate who sets the agenda of the weekly meeting, including juniors
Give every employee a yearly budget to visit one colleague in person
far: Pair each person with a colleague in another time zone to swap one task a week
Publish an internal podcast where teams interview the customers they never meet

prompts.prompt: What could a museum do to attract teenagers?
mid: Let teens curate one room each term and write the labels
Open late on Fridays with a DJ playing music from the exhibit's era
far: Hide unpublished objects in the storage vault and let teens bid for one to be shown
Hire teenagers as paid fact-checkers who mark mistakes on old labels

prompts.prompt: How can a non-profit raise money without asking for donations?
mid: License the non-profit's training materials to companies
Run a paid consulting arm staffed by former beneficiaries
far: Rent out the volunteers' skills as a weekend agency and keep the margin
Auction naming rights to the problems it solves, like a pothole or a broken bench

prompts.prompt: Suggest a new feature for a note-taking app
mid: Notes that expire unless you revisit them
Show which old notes contradict the one you are writing
far: Let a note be sent to your future self only when you return to the same physical place
A trade mode where you swap one anonymous note a day with a stranger in your field
